title: Found youuu
text: “So… you’re in the middle of constructing Filo-tan. In that case… Spear Hero-sama, do you remember?”
“W-what would that be?”
“Ah, guess you might’ve forgotten this part of the flow.”
I tilted my head at Mole’s question while the spear spirit answered something or other. What was that? What exactly was I supposed to have forgotten?

“Well, you see. There was that time Filo got sick and it was a huge ordeal, remember? Afterward, when Ark-sensei came to check on things, he found out about it and prepared a preventive measure, didn’t he? See, she’s not exactly a spirit species, but she’s from the monster bracket, promoted up from a lower-tier event spirit—”

The spear spirit called out to one of the spirits gathered at the celebration as it spoke, and that spirit’s form flickered into view—a faint, star-like impression—and I could tell it was grinning, somehow, despite being made of pure light, in the most unpleasant way imaginable. Found youuu, its expression seemed to say, staring straight at me with a smile that sent chills down my spine.
“Hah!”

I woke with a start from an astonishingly bad aftertaste of a nightmare, indeed. Was that a dream? Or had my consciousness merely drifted off into the spear spirit world for a while? Either way, it was a thoroughly unpleasant experience. After finally solving the problem Ren might’ve caused by tormenting Itsuki and finally going to sleep, this ruined the whole thing, I say.
“Kuu…”
“Mn…? Kitamura, you awake?”
Checking outside, it still seemed dark. Kou and the other Filolial-samas answered me with their heavy eyelids still shut, having noticed I’d woken up.
“Still sleeping, I say.”
“Got it… ‘night… zzz…”

Right. I needed to go back to sleep. A nightmare like that needed to be forgotten. If I remembered it after waking again, I’d have to think about how to handle Mole. Though, at this rate of slave trading, it did feel like I might end up traded off myself. Pondering such things, I drifted back to sleep. Unfortunately, I didn’t fall into the spirit world again.

It was a refreshingly clear morning after turning both Itsuki and Ren into pioneer fairies. Today, over at Father and Big Sister’s place, Filo-tan was supposed to hatch. The preparations were already complete, so what should I do now? I could go check in secretly at Father’s place, but… I should avoid doing anything unnecessary that might lead to an unexpected turn of events. Yes, I had thoroughly learned my lesson from the time, during the very last loop before escaping the cycle, when I peeked in and got called out by the Crimson Swine.
“Motoyasu-sama! What are we doing today?”
“What are we doing? A circus?”
“Still resting, I say. We’re waiting for Father and the others to come back with Filo-tan.”
“The new face… the one Motoyasu-sama treasures so much, is it?”

Hii… did I just sense something terrifying coming off Yuki-chan? Motoyasu, you must cherish your Filolial-samas even more. Getting sick—no, jealous—must absolutely be avoided at all costs. Yuki-chan is… ugh, somehow my brain is refusing to process this. So I must offer as much reassurance as possible. I gently placed my hand under Yuki-chan’s chin and sent her the warmest gaze I could muster.
“That’s right, I say. Filo-tan is a precious Filolial-sama to me, but Yuki-chan is also a precious Filolial-sama, without question.”
“M-Motoyasu-sama…”
“Across so many loops, it was Yuki-chan who stood by me with such devotion and lent me her strength. I have not forgotten that, not even for a moment, I say.”
“Ahh… Yuki is truly blessed. All the other Yukis served Motoyasu-sama so faithfully too, didn’t they.”
“Indeed, I say. Yuki-chan. Every single Filolial-sama is one of a kind, I say.”
“Understood!”

Yuki-chan’s ominous aura dissipated. Whew, indeed. Perhaps it would be wise to introduce her future groom sooner rather than later. But in the very first world, when I introduced Yuki-chan to the White Swan groom Filolial-sama during the loop where I reunited with Fleon-chan, the match hadn’t gone well at all. Yuki-chan is a noble Filolial-sama. Unless a suitor could outrun her, she wouldn’t even acknowledge them as a potential mate. I needed to thoroughly reinforce the Filolial-samas who fancied Yuki-chan. Good, reinforcement it is, I say! Unlike that shady Takt, I would never resort to suspicious drugs or bodily modifications, absolutely not, I say. This time around, Takt was still alive—so I intended to make him regret ever surviving, in the most miserable way possible. Hmm… now, what should I do today, first things first. Sniping Takt’s dragon from a distance and blowing it away sounded good. But approaching carelessly might risk summoning Rival, who could’ve killed herself and reverted back into a spear. Best to finish it off before getting close, I say. Or perhaps I should hunt down every last griffin and unleash all the modified monstrosities Takt had created across the land? No, there was no need to sink to his level. Father had said as much when he dealt with the bandits for sport, so I’d best refrain. Quite the dilemma. Perhaps chipping away at the castle soldiers bit by bit, as a second Fortress of Terror, might also be worthwhile. Surely there were those among them who once tried to mock and torment Father for their own amusement.
“Hey, Elmelo said before that Iwatani should introduce their friend, didn’t she?”
“Panda, is it? Seems it’d be better to go greet her when Father’s around, so that’ll have to wait too, I say.”
“I see~”
“Uu…”
At that moment, Kuro-chan came over looking troubled.
“Hey, do you know where Shadow Saint went? I fell asleep and when I woke up, he was gone.”
Kuu… Kuro-chan. My deepest apologies, I say. Ren has been shipped out as cargo aboard a vessel bound for Zeltoble, indeed. Right about now, he was probably snoring away somewhere on the deck.
“The one Kuro likes is the hero, isn’t it? He probably teleported off somewhere using that Portal power, just like Motoyasu-sama and the others. It’d be best to search for him again later.”
“Uu…”
Nice assist, Yuki-chan, I say.
“Still gonna go look for him.”
It seemed Kuro-chan had simply come to ask whether Ren had shown up at our place.
“You mustn’t go to Naofumi-sama’s place, though—it’s an important time right now, so that’s the one thing you absolutely cannot do.”
“Got it.”
And with that, Kuro-chan dashed off to search for Ren.
“Hey, is there really nothing going on today?”
Kou asked, seeming bored.
“Let’s see. Whether to push Rabbit Guy’s training up another notch or not, I suppose.”
“T-that’s quite alright! I’ve become plenty sturdy already! In fact, I’m thinking it might be about time for a Class Up! Maybe I’ve even gotten control over my Demi-Human transformation—guh.”
Rabbit Guy, apparently attempting a deliberate transformation, had ended up stuck halfway between forms as a half-rabbit beastman.
“Guh… guhhhhhh! Haa… haa…”

He snapped back into his Demi-Human form in an instant. Still couldn’t control it properly, it seemed. Some of his joints had gone slightly out of alignment too, and he seemed to be forcibly correcting them himself, producing an unpleasant cracking sound.
“…Haa.”
I let out a deep sigh while glancing over at Alligator Guy, who was effortlessly carrying luggage nearby.

Alligator Guy, perhaps sensing the situation but deliberately pretending not to notice, set down his load, quietly helped adjust Rabbit Guy’s joints, and then wandered off toward where Éclair was resting.
“Waaahh… fuu.”
Wolf lay sprawled out in his cell, yawning continuously as if taking a nap. The slaves all seemed to have an overabundance of energy they didn’t know what to do with.
“Then Kou wants to go play with Rifana and the others at that village, with Elmelo too!”
“Understood. I’ll send you there right away, I say.”
“Ah, um, actually—the old man who cooks together with Iwatani was just talking with a guest a bit ago? If we’re heading to that village, I think everyone would be happier going together.”
Delicious-food, as Kou apparently called Panda’s adoptive father.
